rule: drop a monotone constraint only if (1) the ratio's denominator can approach zero for a viable firm (interest expense, total debt, revenue), so extreme values stop measuring strength, AND (2) the constraint costs held-out log loss on the inner splits (ablation_summary.csv). Ratios over total assets (roa_net, roa_oper, equity, wc, cash, debt ratios) keep their constraints: total assets >= EUR 1.5MM by construction, and these are the primary reason codes. current_ratio, ar_days, ap_days have near-zero-capable denominators but their constraint costs nothing (cost <= 0 in >= 2 of 3 folds) -> kept.
decided: 2026-11-02 before any outer scoring of GB-08
correction_2026_11_02_1550: The rule text above overstates: ar_days's cost is positive in 2 of 3 folds (+0.000004, +0.000006, -0.000002), so 'cost <= 0 in >= 2 of 3 folds' is false for it; it was kept because the cost is negligible. The rule was written after seeing ablation and shapes, i.e. post hoc. The relax list is unchanged and is what GB-08 used. See decisions.md D-102/D-103.
